newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money in narrower band.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money in narrower band.

text.p: *Volume down to 15.743 billion from 22.175 billion pesos
Manila overnight money was wedged in a narrower band of 10.5625 to 10.53125 percent on Thursday, with the average rate steady at 10.53125 percent, traders said.
Despite the re-offering of the Central Bank's term reverse repos, the market will continue to remain liquid due to the unattractiveness of the instruments, dealers said.
Traders said the government had already issued a formal ruling that these instruments will carry a 20 percent tax.
They would also be classified as deposit substitutes which would subject it to reserve requirements.
"But the ruling created more demand for T-bills (in the secondary market)," a big bank dealer said. "The market is liquid and banks need assets."
Rates could just hover around current levels for as long as the Central Bank maintains its overnight borrowing rate at 10.5 percent, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of eight institutions showed bid rates for three-month bills at 10.60 to 10.70 percent; 11.10 to 11.30 for six months; and 11.45 to 11.70 for one year.
